html:
SMTO-WEB-0034 — The answer came without links to its research

GUID: 6484a075-7706-521f-9a7d-7fedd94e61da
Slug: research-completion-claim-map-missing
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • The Model finished its answer but didn't say which of SMTO's research supports each statement, so SMTO can't check it yet. The research gathered so far is still saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the run to finish. SMTO sends the answer back to the Model and asks it to add the links between its statements and the research. The answer is usually fine once the Model includes those links.
  2. If the run stops, send your question again as a new message. A fresh attempt often includes the links the first one left out.
  3. If it keeps happening, ask the person who manages SMTO to choose a more capable Model in Settings › Setup (model routing). Adding these links is a formatting step that some smaller Models skip.
  4. If the run stops and an unchecked answer is acceptable to you, open the Research proof validation card shown in the run and turn off Enforce this check for this run. This publishes the answer without checking it against the research.

What success looks like

  • The answer appears with source links next to its statements.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with which Model the conversation used. Don't treat an answer published without these links as checked.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof rejected a completion that omits the research claims field, or that supplies an empty claim list without the [[research_summary]] marker.

What this means

  • A proof-enforced completion omits the claims field, or supplies no claims without the research-summary marker. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • A proof-enforced completion omits the claims field, or supplies no claims without the research-summary marker.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the final claims field and the supported summary-only representation.

How to fix it

  • Raised as research_completion_claim_map_missing in _validate_answer. The final completion must include the claims array (CLAIM_SCHEMA) with [[claim_id]] markers referencing current packet subject/fact IDs, or an empty array with [[research_summary]] for a summary-only partial result. Repeated failures usually indicate the configured model is not following the completion tool format.
  • Supply claim references from the current research packet, or use the supported summary-only partial form.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • The completion includes valid claim references or a supported research limitation summary.

What not to do

  • Do not publish unsupported research claims by omitting their required references.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
